description: The client starts a request; the server waits for requests, enforces the rules and answers.
Turns a host name into an IP address; answers are cached for their time-to-live.
Delivers bytes reliably and in order between two machines; it knows nothing about URLs or methods.
A request carries a method, a path, headers and a body; a response carries a status code, headers and a body.
Repeating the request leaves the server in the same state as sending it once, even if the response differs: `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE` are, `POST` is not.
2xx success, 4xx the client must change the request (or, for 429, wait), 5xx the server failed and a later retry may work.
